## TL;DR

Fixed the shell transition defect identified in the latest review. The first-load shell and the routed page now share a Vue transition boundary, so the shell stays mounted while it fades away. The transition is disabled under reduced motion. Added a mounted behavior test for the leaving shell.

## Work and rationale

The prior App template used `v-if` for the loading shell and `v-else` for `RouterView` as sibling states without an enclosing transition. When repository loading ended, Vue removed the complete shell immediately. Although `PageSkeleton` has its own transition, that transition cannot preserve a child after its parent has been removed. The routed view then appeared without an enter effect, which made the change abrupt.

Wrapped both mutually exclusive states in a Vue `Transition` named `page-loading-shell`. This places the lifecycle boundary around the element that switches, allowing Vue to retain the outgoing shell through its leave phase and render the incoming route with the matching enter phase. The application layout and existing PageSkeleton delay/minimum-visible behavior are unchanged.

Added shared shell transition styles with a 140 ms opacity fade. The reduced-motion media query sets the transition to `none`, consistent with the existing motion preference handling. The test mounts a small harness using the same transition name, turns loading off, and asserts that the exiting shell remains present with Vue's leave-active class while the content is mounted. This checks observed transition lifecycle behavior rather than relying only on source-text matching.

## Approaches tried

Inspected the current App template, PageSkeleton transition, and the existing loading-skeleton test suite. The defect was localized to App's conditional parent lifecycle. Kept the fix at that boundary instead of changing PageSkeleton's own transition because the issue was that its parent disappeared before its child transition could complete.

## Challenges and blockers

The initial CSS patch context did not match the actual loading-shell rules in `style.css`; I read the current block and placed the new transition rules beside those rules. No remaining blocker is known. The scoped RepoOS check is still required before handoff.

## Key learnings

A component-level leave transition is insufficient when an ancestor's conditional rendering removes the whole subtree. The transition must wrap the condition that replaces the loading shell with the route. A lifecycle test should verify the outgoing element remains during its leave phase, since matching class names in source alone would not catch the original unmounting problem.
